'''Sasha Mendjan''' (born 1 June 1978) is a molecular biologist, principal investigator at the [[Institute of Molecular Biotechnology]] (IMBA) of the Austrian Academy of Sciences and tenure-track assistant professor in synthetic tissue biology at the [[Medical University of Vienna]].<ref name="MedUni2024" /> His research focuses on human [[Heart development|cardiogenesis]], [[Stem cell|stem cell biology]],  and disease modelling, particularly through the development of self-organizing [[Organoid|cardiac organoids]] known as “cardioids”.<ref name="IMBABio">{{cite web |title=Sasha Mendjan |url=https://www.technologynetworks.com/tn/editor/sasha-mendjan-phd |website=Technology Networks |access-date=2026-03-19}}</ref><ref name="MedUni2024">{{cite web |title=Sasha Mendjan takes up tenure-track assistant professorship at MedUni Vienna |url=https://www.meduniwien.ac.at/web/en/about-us/news/2024/news-in-march-2024/sasha-mendjan-takes-up-tenure-track-assistant-professorship-at-meduni-vienna-1/ |publisher=Medical University of Vienna |date=2024-03-01 |access-date=2026-03-19}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Mendjan was born in 1978 in [[Zemun]], then part of the [[Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia]].<ref name="CV">{{cite web |title=Biographical sketch – Sasha Mendjan |url=https://www.oeaw.ac.at/fileadmin/Institute/IMBA/scientific/research/Mendjan/CV_Mendjan_General_070922.pdf |publisher=Institute of Molecular Biotechnology |access-date=2026-03-19}}</ref> He studied biology and biochemistry at [[LMU Munich]], completing diploma studies in biology and a diploma thesis in biochemistry.<ref name="CV" />

He obtained his Ph.D. at the [[European Molecular Biology Laboratory]] (EMBL) and [[Heidelberg University]], where he worked on the chromosomal regulation of transcription under the supervision of [[Asifa Akhtar]].<ref name="IMBABio" /><ref name="CV" />

Mendjan subsequently carried out postdoctoral research at the [[University of Cambridge]], where he developed differentiation systems from human pluripotent stem cells into mesodermal lineages, enabling mechanistic studies of early developmental processes.<ref name="IMBABio" /><ref name="MedUni2024" />

== Research and career ==
In 2015, Mendjan established his own research group at the [[Institute of Molecular Biotechnology]] (IMBA) in Vienna.<ref name="CV2">{{cite web |title=Biographical sketch – Sasha Mendjan (2024) |url=https://www.oeaw.ac.at/fileadmin/Institute/IMBA/scientific/research/Mendjan/CV_Mendjan_SM220524.pdf |publisher=Institute of Molecular Biotechnology |access-date=2026-03-19}}</ref> His laboratory investigates the molecular and cellular mechanisms of human heart development, congenital heart disease, and regeneration.<ref name="IMBABio" />

A central contribution of his group is the development of “cardioids”, self-organising cardiac organoids derived from human pluripotent stem cells that recapitulate structural and functional features of the developing human heart including the self-organization into chamber-like structures, modelling this aspect of heart biology more closely than other cardiac organoid systems.<ref name="IMBABio" /><ref name="Cardioids2021">{{cite web |title=Human self-organizing cardiac organoids mimic the architecture of a heart chamber |url=https://www.azolifesciences.com/news/20210521/Human-self-organizing-cardiac-organoids-mimic-the-architecture-of-a-heart-chamber.aspx |website=AZo Life Sciences |date=2021-05-21 |access-date=2026-03-19}}</ref> These models have enabled the study of cardiac lineage specification, chamber formation, and disease mechanisms in vitro, addressing limitations in modelling human heart development.<ref name="Cardioids2021" />

The Mendjan laboratory has further expanded these systems into multi-chamber organoids that reproduce interactions between cardiac compartments and can be used to investigate congenital defects and drug responses.<ref name="IMBANews">{{cite web |title=A complete multi-chamber organoid to study and treat heart diseases |url=https://www.invitrojobs.com/index.php/en/news/news-archive/item/6254-imba-a-complete-multi-chamber-organoid-to-study-and-treat-heart-diseases |website=InVitro Jobs |date=2023-12-01 |access-date=2026-03-19}}</ref>
